quality_assessment: Chapter is generally accurate and comprehensive, but lacks coverage of the ignore hierarchy interaction and has a minor terminology inconsistency with exclude patterns. The content is well-structured with excellent examples, but could benefit from explaining how globs interact with the broader ignore system.

issues.description: Chapter states globs 'always override automatic filtering' but doesn't explain the full precedence hierarchy from features.json
issues.current_content: **Important:** Glob patterns always override automatic filtering from `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and other sources.
issues.should_add: Explain the complete ignore hierarchy: Override patterns (--include/--exclude) > Custom ignore files > .ignore > .gitignore > .git/info/exclude > Global gitignore > Explicit ignore files > Hidden file detection
issues.fix_suggestion: Add a subsection explaining where --glob/-g fits in the precedence order. Clarify that --glob is an 'override pattern' at the top of the hierarchy.

issues.description: Chapter mentions performance but doesn't explain the 7 optimized glob strategies that ripgrep uses internally
issues.should_add: Optional advanced note about how ripgrep optimizes glob patterns into different matching strategies (literal, basename_literal, extension, prefix, suffix, required_extension, regex) for better performance
issues.fix_suggestion: Add an optional 'Advanced: Glob Optimization' callout box explaining that ripgrep automatically optimizes simple patterns (like '*.rs') into faster matching strategies than complex regex patterns

issues.description: The section title says 'Include and Exclude Patterns' but there's no explicit 'include' flag - all patterns are includes by default, with '!' prefix for excludes
issues.current_content:
## Include and Exclude Patterns

Prefix a glob with `!` to exclude files that match:
issues.should_be:
## Including and Excluding Files

By default, glob patterns include files. Prefix a glob with `!` to exclude files that match:
issues.fix_suggestion: Retitle the section to avoid implying there are separate include/exclude flags. Clarify that -g/--glob handles both cases based on presence of '!' prefix.

issues.description: Chapter states 'Empty alternatives like {,c} are not supported' which is confirmed in source, but should note this is a known limitation
issues.current_content: **Note:** Empty alternatives like `{,c}` are not supported. This is a ripgrep extension beyond standard `.gitignore` syntax.
issues.should_be: **Note:** Empty alternatives like `{,c}` are not currently supported (as of ripgrep 14.1+). Brace expansion is a ripgrep extension beyond standard `.gitignore` syntax.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add version context to indicate this is a current limitation, not a documentation error. This helps readers understand it might be supported in future versions.

issues.description: Chapter documents --iglob and --glob-case-insensitive but doesn't mention the negated form --no-glob-case-insensitive
issues.should_add: Mention that --glob-case-insensitive has a negated form --no-glob-case-insensitive that can restore case-sensitive matching
issues.fix_suggestion: Add example: 'Use --no-glob-case-insensitive to restore case-sensitive matching after earlier use of --glob-case-insensitive'

issues.description: Example shows both 'test' and 'tests' exclusions, but doesn't explain why both are needed
issues.should_be:
### Exclude Test Directories
```bash
# Exclude both common test directory naming conventions
rg -g '!**/test/**' -g '!**/tests/**' pattern
```
issues.fix_suggestion: Add comment explaining that different projects use different naming conventions (test vs tests), so both exclusions may be needed for comprehensive filtering

positive_aspects: Excellent structure progressing from basic to advanced concepts
Comprehensive coverage of glob syntax with clear examples for each feature
Good use of visual markers (✅/❌) to highlight correct vs incorrect usage
Practical examples section is very helpful and covers real-world use cases
Clear explanation of common pitfall with directory matching (foo vs foo/**)
Comparison table with type filters provides good context for when to use each approach
Performance considerations section helps users make informed choices
Preview with --files flag is a valuable troubleshooting tip
Gitignore compatibility section helps users transfer existing knowledge
Escaping metacharacters section addresses a common pain point
improvement_suggestions: Add a quick reference box at the top summarizing key glob wildcards and special syntax
Include a troubleshooting subsection for common glob mistakes beyond just the directory pitfall
Add cross-references to automatic filtering chapter to help readers understand when to use each approach
Consider adding a 'glob patterns cheatsheet' table for quick reference
Add examples showing how globs interact with --hidden and --no-ignore flags
Include a note about shell glob expansion and why quotes are important around glob patterns
Add example showing how to use globs to search only in recently modified files (though this requires combining with other features)
Consider adding a visual diagram showing the precedence hierarchy for ignore patterns
